issue_context.title: Support stage-3 class static blocks
issue_context.body:
<!--

If then, your issue will be fixed more quickly.

**Describe the feature**

Support Stage-3 proposal class static blocks.

**Babel plugin or link to the feature description**

https://babeljs.io/docs/en/babel-plugin-proposal-class-static-block

**Additional context**
Add any other context about the problem here.

TypeScript 4.4 supports class static blocks (https://devblogs.microsoft.com/typescript/announcing-typescript-4-4-rc/#static-blocks)
comments: @kdy1 If this feature is needed, can I work on this?
Of course. Thank you a lot!
@sosukesuzuki have you started working on this? I'm eager to support it given that TS 4.4 is now out. If not, I can start working on it on Monday.
I've started to work! I'll do the rest of the work today.
@sosukesuzuki great work. Thanks for implementing this, @sosukesuzuki! 🙂
We should implement transforms for static blocks so the code can be used while targeting old browsers.
Oh sorry, I forgot about this. I'll work on this.
@kdy1 Is there any documentation useful for writing transforms? I've read the code for a while, but it's difficult...
Yep, I am faced with this too, because code base is big (some of use is new in rust), maybe will be great to create small examples for popular cases, like replace `Hello world!` on `Hello swc!`.
@kdy1 Thank you for telling me! I'll try again.
This closed issue has been automatically locked because it had no new activity for a month. If you are running into a similar issue, please create a new issue with the steps to reproduce. Thank you.

review_comments:
To handle nested declarations, you have to call `declaration.fold_children_with(self)`
like

```rust
let declaration = declaration.fold_children_with(self);
```

This is different from babel, because the ownership model of rust is designed to forbid modifications like it.
@kdy1 Does any cache exist for these fixtures tests? I'm confusing because sometimes when I update the fixtures, it is not reflected in the test results...

If you add or remove the fixture, you have to `touch` the rust file containing `#[testing::fixture]`.

(It's annoying, but it is far better than controlling tests using environment variables.)

You can simply return `static_blocks()` instead.

e.g.

```rust
&|_t| static_blocks(),
```
Thanks. I've fixed this file for testing with both `static_blocks` and `class_properties`.
